tess-cs: Heads up 020: Ivan at Fleetly reports intermittent 401s followed by short 429 storms during their SDK onboarding. They rolled a new ephemeral token refresh that fires every 3s. Sample from their mobile logs: `time=2026-03-21T14:12:03Z level=warn auth=401 req=req-abc123 reason=token_stale` then later `time=2026-03-21T14:12:05Z level=info gateway=429 req=req-abc123 reason=burst_backpressure`
ivan-customer: Confirmed. We're getting ~1/15 requests 401 and then a spike of 429s lasting ~8-12s. Tokens are minted by our edge auth and TTL is 8s. We create a new SDK client per background job on the device.
noah-eng: Quick triage questions: are devices clock-synced? are you opening new TCP/HTTP connections per client? which region are you targeting? Also, can you paste your SDK init snippet?
ivan-customer: Devices use NTP, roughly in sync. We do new client per job. Targeting us-west. Snippet: ```py from redwood import Client c = Client(api_key=ephemeral, region='us-west', retries=1) c.generate(prompt) ```
noah-eng: Hypothesis: very short TTL + per-job client creation -> auth service sees many simultaneous token exchange/preflight requests and some tokens are used just before they're valid/after expiry (401). The edge gateway then rate-limits the downstream to protect capacity, returning 429. Also per-connection TLS handshakes add overhead when you spawn many clients quickly.
ingest-bot: extracted logs for req-abc123: auth-service returned 401 for 5 requests in 3s window, gateway returned 429 for 89 requests in 10s window.
noah-eng: Remediations: 1) increase ephemeral TTL to ~45-60s so refresh frequency drops; 2) implement a short-lived local token cache per device process and reuse a single SDK client instance (singleton) instead of creating per job; 3) add jitter to refresh schedule (e.g., random +/- 0-4000ms); 4) honor Retry-After header on 429s and implement exponential backoff; 5) optionally enable connection pooling in the SDK (pool=true) or let the SDK manage keepalive connections.
ivan-customer: If we bump TTL to 60s we'll reduce token churn but we can't change all devices immediately. Any quick mitigations we can apply server-side?
tess-cs: Ops can add a short soft-exemption for their IP blocks during testing. ops-tilly, can you help?
ops-tilly: Yep. I'll add a temporary lenient burst window for fleetly's src CIDR for 45 minutes while you test. I'll log the rule id.
noah-eng: Also recommend a tiny server-side grace window for newly minted tokens: accept tokens issued up to 2s before validity and up to 2s after expiry (configurable). That helps slots where devices have small clock skew or network delay.
ivan-customer: I'll roll a canary with TTL=60s + single-client change and jitter. Anything else for region routing?
noah-eng: Set region='auto' or remove hard-coded region if you have global users; if you need specific region mapping, ensure the SDK is created once per region shard rather than per job.
tess-cs: I'll book a 30-min troubleshooting + metrics watch tomorrow at 9:00 AM PT. Action items: tess-cs -> coordinate call; ivan -> deploy canary with TTL and client reuse; noah -> standby to watch logs; ops-tilly -> soft-exemption & monitor.
ivan-customer: Thanks 64f I'll update before the call.
noah-eng: Quick example backoff pseudo-code for client refresh: ```py # add jitter & backoff import random def schedule_refresh(base_s=30): jitter = random.uniform(0,4) schedule = base_s + jitter return schedule # on 429 apply exponential backoff ```
tess-cs: Noted renewal risk: currently flagged as "watching"; if still flapping after enablement we'll escalate to renewals team.
ops-tilly: Rule added: soft-burst-exempt fleetly-cidr (expires in 45m) rule-id=soft-9876.
ivan-customer: Appreciate the help everyone. I'll post results in this thread once the canary has run.
